name: Memvid
tagline: Portable single-file memory layer for AI agents — no database.
description: Memvid stores an agent's knowledge as compressed 'Smart Frames' in a single portable .mv2 file that bundles data, embeddings, and the search index — replacing vector databases and complex RAG pipelines. It offers sub-5ms retrieval, append-only versioned storage, and runs fully offline. The format is model-agnostic and multimodal.
insight: Open-sourced under Apache-2.0 with ~16k GitHub stars; commercialized by Memvid, Inc. behind the .mv2 file format.

modelSupport.notes: Storage + retrieval layer; works with any embedding model and LLM.

edge: No database or infra to run — memory ships as one portable, offline .mv2 file with sub-5ms retrieval, unlike server-based memory layers.
cons: Video-frame approach is novel and debated
Best for embed/edge, not multi-writer servers
